It definitely feels like there is an external significance to what I'm doing.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about hearing your brother's voice, is it something you hear only when you're working on your paintings or do you hear it at other times as well?\n\nPatient: I really only hear his voice when I'm out in the workshop late at night, working hard on these canvases. It's tied directly to those times when I have all this high energy to paint, and on the rare days when my energy dips back to normal, I don't hear him at all.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other types of perceptions, such as seeing things that others can't, smelling something unusual, or feeling sensations on your skin, especially when you're working on your paintings or hearing your brother's voice?\n\nPatient: No, I don't see anything that isn't there, and I've never smelled or felt anything unusual on my skin. The only thing like that is hearing my brother's voice when I'm out working in the garage late at night. Aside from his voice, my other senses are completely normal.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how you distinguish between the voice of your brother that you hear and your own thoughts, is it clearly your brother's voice or could it be your own mind thinking about what he might say?\n\nPatient: It is absolutely his voice, sounding as clear as if he were standing right behind me in the workshop saying, \"keep going, they're watching.\" It doesn't feel like my own thoughts at all, even though I rationally know he is actually hours away at home or getting his chemotherapy.\n\nDoctor: How long have you been experiencing these feelings of importance about your paintings and hearing your brother's voice, and have they been constant or have they changed over time?\n\nPatient: This has been going on for about two months, starting right after my friend passed away and my brother got sick. It isn't constant, though—it only happens when I'm really wound up and energetic with my projects, and on the rare days my energy dips back to normal, the thoughts and voices fade away.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned that these experiences and the voice of your brother seem to be closely tied to your energy levels and mood, can you tell me more about what happens to these feelings of importance and the voice when your energy is low or you're not working on your paintings?\n\nPatient: When my energy dips back to normal, those intense ideas about the secret messages in my paintings just fade into the background and don't feel as urgent or real. It's like the thoughts and the voice only show up when I'm really wound up and working on the art.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods where these beliefs about your paintings and the voice of your brother seemed completely irrational or unrealistic to you, even if only for a short time?\n\nPatient: On the rare days when my energy dips back toward normal, those thoughts and my brother's voice fade into the background and feel less intense. Most of the time, it doesn't feel unrealistic at all.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever have moments, even if briefly, where you question the reality of the messages in your paintings or the voice of your brother, or do you always feel certain about their significance?\n\nPatient: Most of the time, especially when my energy is high, the messages in my art and my brother's voice feel absolutely real and urgent. I never had these ideas or heard those voices at all before I got so wound up and driven over the last couple of months.\n\nDoctor: When you're in that lower energy state and the thoughts about the messages in your paintings and your brother's voice seem less intense, do you think that maybe you were mistaken about their importance or do you still believe they could be real but just not as pressing at that moment?\n\nPatient: When my energy dips, those thoughts and my brother's voice fade into the background and don't feel intense or urgent at all. But as soon as my energy gets high again, they feel absolutely real and true to me, even if others say it's far-fetched. It really depends on how wound up I am feeling at the time.\n\nDoctor: Do you think it's possible that your high energy and stress over the past couple of months, combined with your brother's illness and your friend's passing, might be contributing to these intense beliefs about your paintings and hearing your brother's voice?"

It definitely feels like there is an external significance to what I'm doing.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about hearing your brother's voice, is it something you hear only when you're working on your paintings or do you hear it at other times as well?\n\nPatient: I really only hear his voice when I'm out in the workshop late at night, working hard on these canvases. It's tied directly to those times when I have all this high energy to paint, and on the rare days when my energy dips back to normal, I don't hear him at all.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any other types of perceptions, such as seeing things that others can't, smelling something unusual, or feeling sensations on your skin, especially when you're working on your paintings or hearing your brother's voice?\n\nPatient: No, I don't see anything that isn't there, and I've never smelled or felt anything unusual on my skin. The only thing like that is hearing my brother's voice when I'm out working in the garage late at night. Aside from his voice, my other senses are completely normal.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how you distinguish between the voice of your brother that you hear and your own thoughts, is it clearly your brother's voice or could it be your own mind thinking about what he might say?\n\nPatient: It is absolutely his voice, sounding as clear as if he were standing right behind me in the workshop saying, \"keep going, they're watching.\" It doesn't feel like my own thoughts at all, even though I rationally know he is actually hours away at home or getting his chemotherapy.\n\nDoctor: How long have you been experiencing these feelings of importance about your paintings and hearing your brother's voice, and have they been constant or have they changed over time?\n\nPatient: This has been going on for about two months, starting right after my friend passed away and my brother got sick. It isn't constant, though—it only happens when I'm really wound up and energetic with my projects, and on the rare days my energy dips back to normal, the thoughts and voices fade away.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned that these experiences and the voice of your brother seem to be closely tied to your energy levels and mood, can you tell me more about what happens to these feelings of importance and the voice when your energy is low or you're not working on your paintings?\n\nPatient: When my energy dips back to normal, those intense ideas about the secret messages in my paintings just fade into the background and don't feel as urgent or real. I don't hear my brother's voice at all during those times either. It's like the thoughts and the voice only show up when I'm really wound up and working on the art.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any periods where these beliefs about your paintings and the voice of your brother seemed completely irrational or unrealistic to you, even if only for a short time?\n\nPatient: On the rare days when my energy dips back toward normal, those thoughts and my brother's voice fade into the background and feel less intense. But overall, especially when I am wound up, they still feel absolutely true and real to me, even though my wife tells me it's far-fetched. Most of the time, it doesn't feel unrealistic at all.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever have moments, even if briefly, where you question the reality of the messages in your paintings or the voice of your brother, or do you always feel certain about their significance?\n\nPatient: Most of the time, especially when my energy is high, the messages in my art and my brother's voice feel absolutely real and urgent. I do have brief moments where it contradicts logic, like knowing my brother is actually hours away getting chemo, or when my energy dips and the intensity fades a bit. But overall, the feeling that my work carries a major, real significance remains incredibly strong.\n\nDoctor: When you're not feeling as energetic or wound up about your paintings, do you think that maybe the messages and your brother's voice might not be as real or important as they seem when you're in that high-energy state?\n\nPatient: Yes, that's exactly right. On the rare days when my energy dips back toward normal, those thoughts about the secret messages and hearing my brother's voice do fade into the background and feel much less intense. I never had these ideas or heard those voices at all before I got so wound up and driven over the last couple of months.\n\nDoctor: When you're in that lower energy state and the thoughts about the messages in your paintings and your brother's voice seem less intense, do you think that maybe you were mistaken about their importance or do you still believe they could be real but just not as pressing at that moment?\n\nPatient: When my energy dips, those thoughts and my brother's voice fade into the background and don't feel intense or urgent at all. But as soon as my energy gets high again, they feel absolutely real and true to me, even if others say it's far-fetched. It really depends on how wound up I am feeling at the time.\n\nDoctor: Do you think it's possible that your high energy and stress over the past couple of months, combined with your brother's illness and your friend's passing, might be contributing to these intense beliefs about your paintings and hearing your brother's voice?\n\nPatient: The timing fits perfectly, as I never had these ideas about secret messages or heard my brother's voice before I got so wound up and driven with these projects over the last couple of months. On the rare days when my energy dips back toward normal, those thoughts and voices fade into the background, though they still feel absolutely real to me when it's happening.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about your mood when you're not experiencing these high-energy states and the voices or intense beliefs about your paintings, do you feel sad, empty, or disconnected from things that usually bring you pleasure?\n\nPatient: When my energy levels drop, I don't really feel sad or empty; things just feel a lot quieter and closer to normal. I haven't experienced those kinds of low feelings recently, it is more just a calm break from all the excitement.\n\nDoctor: When you're in those quieter, more normal states, do you feel like you're missing the excitement and energy of your projects, or is it more of a relief to not be feeling so wound up and driven all the time?\n\nPatient: I'm not really sure, as I haven't thought about it that way. I just know that when my energy drops, everything gets a lot quieter and those intense thoughts and voices fade away.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that if your energy levels and drive for your projects were to remain consistently high, the intensity of your beliefs about the secret messages in your paintings and the voice of your brother would also remain constant, or might they eventually fade even if your energy stays up?\n\nPatient: I definitely think they are closely linked, because the ideas about the messages and hearing my brother's voice only started when I got so wound up and busy with my projects. I also haven't been paying much attention to eating or my appetite lately because I get so completely focused on my art.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely sad, hopeless, or had no interest in activities you usually enjoy, lasting for at least two weeks?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't really ever experienced a period where I felt extremely sad, hopeless, or lost interest in my usual activities for that long. My life has generally been pretty steady up until this recent burst of energy and focus on my art.\n\nDoctor: Have you noticed any significant changes in your self-esteem or feelings of grandiosity, especially when you're in those high-energy states and deeply involved in your painting projects?\n\nPatient: Yes, during those times I feel a massive surge in energy and a powerful sense of purpose, like I'm completely pumped up. I become absolutely convinced that my paintings carry highly important, hidden messages meant for the President and national leaders to help save our town's soul. It feels like a special duty I have, even if other people dismiss it or don't understand the scale of what I'm doing.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that when you're in these high-energy states, your beliefs about the importance of your paintings and the messages they contain might be inflated or exaggerated, or do you believe they are entirely realistic and justified?\n\nPatient: While my wife and others tell me that these ideas are far-fetched or exaggerated, they feel absolutely real, urgent, and completely justified to me when my energy is high. I genuinely believe that these paintings carry a crucial message that the people in charge need to see.\n\nDoctor: Do you think your high energy and feelings of grandeur about your paintings could be contributing to your beliefs about their importance, or do you believe these beliefs would remain strong even if your energy and mood were more stable?\n\nPatient: I definitely think they are connected, because these intense beliefs about my paintings and hearing my brother's voice only happen when I am highly energetic and wound up. On the rare days when my energy levels dip back to normal, those thoughts and voices fade into the background. I never had any of these ideas before this high-energy period started.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that if your energy levels and drive for your projects were to return to a normal, stable state, you would still believe as strongly in the secret messages in your paintings and the voice of your brother?\n\nPatient: I don't think I would, because I never had these ideas about secret messages or heard my brother's voice before I got so wound up and driven over the last couple of months. They are definitely tied to my energy. On the rare days when my energy dips back toward normal, those thoughts and the voice do fade into the background.\n\nDoctor: Do you think that your beliefs about the secret messages in your paintings and the voice of your brother would still be considered delusional if your energy levels and mood were more stable, or are they only problematic when you're in a high-energy state?"
